name: Abdon
overview: Abdon was a male judge of Israel known for his leadership and governance. He was the son of Hillel and served as a judge over Israel for eight years, as recorded in Judges 12:13. His role as a judge highlights his importance in the period of Israel's tribal leadership.
namesAndTitles: The name Abdon means 'servant,' which reflects a humble and dedicated role. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance related to service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Abdon was the son of Hillel. Beyond this, no other family relationships or tribal affiliations are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Abdon's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a judge who led Israel for eight years, providing stability and guidance during a turbulent period. His leadership is noted in Judges 12:13, marking him as one of the key figures who upheld God's justice and order among the Israelites after the initial conquest of the Promised Land.
